rubrics.title: Lab 10 — Analyze Your Twitter/X Data with Python

criteria.description: Lecture — lecture10.ipynb: complete the shared dummy-data insert, two updates, delete, and three query exercises, with executed code and outputs. This is one 30-point criterion; no separate lecture AI Use or overall Summary.

Lab Questions — lab10.ipynb: Q1–Q4, 10 points each. Include the actual query, executable Python, required output, and brief Markdown findings. Q1: the 20 most-liked tweets, complete text and likes in a pandas table. Q2: ten most-followed users, bar chart of usernames and follower counts. Q3: common profile locations based on users, bar chart. Q4: up to ten popular hashtags, bar chart; explain a successful query with no hashtags in Markdown instead. No separate overall Summary. Read the student's existing lab8.tweet_collection without changing it.

AI Use — in lab10.ipynb after Q4: 3–4 sentences stating the approved tools used and how they helped, a limitation or check, and a privacy risk or precaution. Approved tools: MongoDB built-in AI and Gemini inside Colab. Confirmed unapproved AI use results in zero for the entire assignment; repeated violations will be reported to the JMU Honor Council.

Submission & Source Access: correct assigned GitHub repository root URL and a complete working MongoDB connection string on separate lines in private Canvas. Both lecture10.ipynb and lab10.ipynb at the repository root on main, accessible to the instructor and saved directly from Colab with outputs, Created using Colab, and working Open in Colab links. Credential exposure is a separate one-time 20-point deduction, floored at zero; do not double-deduct the same exposure under this criterion.
